answer: Cross-chain binding at the canyon: one identity must hold ≥0.01 ETH on two chains for 30 days. Trellis enforces it by linking both addresses through a single signed attestation, so a farm needs 2n funded wallets, not n. The ripple is cost: doubling identities doubles capital at risk simultaneously across chains, with no cheap exit. Empirical data shows farms abandon this at ~40 wallets because locked capital outpaces reward. It works because sybil cost scales linearly with identity count while honest users pay once.
